result.title: Improved Training of Strong Stochastic Flow Maps
result.summary: Stochastic flow maps promise few-step sampling of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) by learning to directly jump between times along the solution path, yet training these models to learn this solution map remains difficult. The primary obstacle is the Brownian path itself: it is an infinite-dimensional object which needs to be passed to the neural network and is nowhere differentiable, which makes the implementation of derivative-based losses that power the state-of-the-art deterministic flow maps just out of reach. We identify two core design principles which address these issues: a) represent the Brownian path with a basis which carries higher-order local information, and b) train with an objective that forces the network to use the full representation of the path, not just the first order. To address this, we leverage the shifted Legendre polynomial expansion with a Wong-Zakai styled objective, unlocking derivative-based losses. Finally, we propose a recipe for fine-tuning large pre-trained flow models into strong stochastic flow maps. We ablate through this design space on several toy problems and use our findings to transform a large flow model into a strong stochastic flow map on ImageNet, achieving roughly a three-fold improvement in FD-DINOv2 over SSFM at four NFE.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究随机流映射的少步采样训练难题，提出用带高阶局部信息的基（shifted Legendre 多项式展开）表示 Brownian 路径，并配合 Wong-Zakai 式目标使基于导数的损失可用，同时给出把大型预训练流模型微调为强随机流映射的方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用高阶基表示随机路径、并设计目标迫使网络使用完整表示而非仅一阶信息」的思路，可能可供核查 latent 推理轨迹的表示与监督设计能否抑制信息坍缩；但与 VLM 推理本身无直接关系。
